title: 4.4 Congruence and Transformations

icans: I can describe a congruence transformation that maps one figure onto another.
I can decide whether two figures are congruent.
I can use the theorems about reflections in parallel and intersecting lines.

vocab: figures with the same size and __________
a transformation that ____________ length and angle measure (a translation, reflection, rotation, or a composition of them)

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Congruence: two figures are congruent if and only if there is a _______________ of rigid motions that maps one onto the other.

blocks.stem: Describe a congruence transformation that maps △ABC to △DEF: A(1, 1), B(3, 1), C(1, 4) and D(1, −1), E(3, −1), F(1, −4).
Describe a congruence transformation that maps △ABC with A(−4, 1), B(−2, 1), C(−4, 3) onto △PQR with P(4, −3), Q(2, −3), R(4, −1).

notes: Reflections in Parallel Lines Theorem: reflecting in two parallel lines is the same as a _______________, twice the distance between the lines.
Reflections in Intersecting Lines Theorem: reflecting in two intersecting lines is the same as a _______________ about their intersection by twice the angle between them.

blocks.stem: Reflect (0, 2) in the line x = 1, then reflect the image in x = 4. What single transformation does the same thing?
A figure is reflected in x = −1 and then in x = 2. Describe the single transformation.

tickets.stem: Is a figure congruent to its image after a rotation?
Two lines intersect at a 25° angle. Reflecting in one and then the other is the same as what?
